title: Wes Helvey's band in Cincinnati and Leonard Gay
summary: After Madison he played in Cincinnati with Wes Helvey's band, then went back to Wisconsin with saxophonist Leonard Gay, a Trumbauer devotee.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: No, it's very practical. Well I think -- let's see -- where did we leave off? We left off where you came back home and you decided to learn to read and then you went out again --
It's Madison where I decided to learn to read.
-- and write. But I did go back out again. But I had played with several other guys that
had played with a band called Elvey (PHONETIC) in Cincinnati.
Yeah, Les Hilton -- you know about him -- hey?
Well I've looked it up and --

He's got a really good band. A very good band. And then he went to ______, I went back out there. Went back out to Wisconsin. You know, and that's -- in that band it was Lenoard Jay (PHONETIC). That's him -- that's his picture right there. Look there's (inaudible).

Here -- he's here in the center section (inaudible) the one in the middle (inaudible). He just died I understand a couple -- a month or two ago -- around this time. So he was -- he was a very good saxophone player. He started out like -- like a trombone.

He copied Frankie -- he was cracy about Frankie TRUMBAER. He would play all them solos that Frankie -- and things like that. And then -- at the end of that -- we -- we joined Steve Rebb's (PHONETIC) band.
